moduleSource.title: Exercise and Athletic Performance — HMB, betaine, glutamine, bicarbonate and tart-cherry sections
moduleSource.licenseNote: Brief original factual paraphrases with NIH attribution and canonical source links. No source tables, figures, photos or full articles reproduced; no open licence asserted. Publisher update April 1, 2024 is shown on the inspected page; extraction/review occurred on 2026-10-08.

sourceCaptureMethod: Primary NIH ODS pages inspected through the web tool, including the displayed April 1, 2024 update. No raw HTML archive retained and no direct-download attempt or capture hash claimed.
sourceLocators: HMB: efficacy, safety and distinct forms in implications for use
Betaine: efficacy, short-duration evidence and insufficient safety assessment
Glutamine: specific six-week strength-study result, safety and differing recovery context
Sodium bicarbonate: conflicting results, individual variation, gastrointestinal distress and sodium exposure
Tart or sour cherry: product/population-specific recovery studies, safety limitations and no consensus
reviewMethod: Compared brief original observations with the named primary NIH sections; stable identities, byte-pinned transcriptions, explicit unknown regimen/magnitude and source/schema checks before factual publication. No independent human or clinical review.
